# Design Tokens Reference

## 1. System Overview

This design tokens reference is part of the Infomaniak Design System. It contains the default resolved token values for the design system, accounting for light and dark theme variants. Use this file as the definitive reference when building UI components. The values shown represent the default product; when building for a specific product (calendar, mail, swisstransfer, etc.), the build system automatically resolves the same token names to the correct product-specific colors.

## 2. Semantic Tokens (The Usage)

| Token Name | Light Value | Dark Value | CSS Variable | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| blur.none | 0px | 0px | var(--esds-blur-none) | No blur; sharp, unaffected element. |
| blur.xs | 4px | 4px | var(--esds-blur-xs) | Extra-small blur for subtle focus effects. |
| blur.sm | 8px | 8px | var(--esds-blur-sm) | Small blur for soft focus and light depth. |
| blur.md | 12px | 12px | var(--esds-blur-md) | Medium blur for moderate focus and depth. |
| blur.lg | 16px | 16px | var(--esds-blur-lg) | Large blur for prominent depth and focus. |
| blur.xl | 24px | 24px | var(--esds-blur-xl) | Extra-large blur for strong focus effects. |
| blur.2xl | 40px | 40px | var(--esds-blur-2xl) | 2x-large blur for heavy depth effects. |
| blur.3xl | 64px | 64px | var(--esds-blur-3xl) | 3x-large blur for maximum blur effects. |
| border.none.width | 0px | 0px | var(--esds-border-none-width) | No border width. |
| border.xs.width | 1px | 1px | var(--esds-border-xs-width) | Extra-small border width for fine hairline borders. |
| border.sm.width | 2px | 2px | var(--esds-border-sm-width) | Small border width for subtle outlines. |
| border.md.width | 3px | 3px | var(--esds-border-md-width) | Medium border width for default element outlines. |
| border.lg.width | 4px | 4px | var(--esds-border-lg-width) | Large border width for emphasized outlines. |
| color.background.elevation.sunken | #f1f5f9 | #020618 | var(--esds-color-background-elevation-sunken) | Background for sunken, recessed surfaces below the base level. |
| color.background.elevation.surface | #fff | #192334 | var(--esds-color-background-elevation-surface) | Background for the default surface level, the base UI layer. |

## 4. AI Implementation Directives

- **Always use CSS variables** in implementation. Never hard-code hex or dimension values.
- **Prefer Tier 2 (Semantic) tokens** for all component styling. Only use Tier 3 (Component) tokens when they explicitly exist for the element you are building.
- **Never reference Tier 1 (Primitive) tokens directly** in component code; they exist only for alias resolution and designer reference.
- **Theme awareness**: The design system supports `light` and `dark` modes. Use the `data-esds-theme` attribute or corresponding modifier CSS file to apply themes.
- **Portable product tokens**: When building components for a specific product (calendar, mail, swisstransfer, etc.), always use the token names exactly as shown in this file (e.g., `color.background.brand` with `var(--esds-color-background-brand)`). The build system automatically resolves these to the correct product-specific colors. **Never** use product-specific token names such as `color.background.brand.calendar` directly in component code. **Never** create separate component variants or branches per product when the same semantic token exists. All products share the same token API — only the resolved values differ.

# Designers Guide/Android/Android - Technical Limitations

> **Goal:** determine how the components can be used and any related constraints.

**Goal:** determine how the components can be used and any related constraints.

---

## Overall backward compatibility

- **Jetpack Compose** keeps components compatible regardless of the OS, unlike Apple.

## App Bars

- **XR (Mixed Reality)**, intended for virtual reality headsets → to be removed from the entire
  kit.
- The **left-aligned label** version can use a **hamburger menu** instead of the arrow.
- 3 parameters: **nav**, **title**, **action**.
  - **Nav** → free.
  - **Action** → free, but **max 3 icons** recommended (more is possible but discouraged).

## Avatars

- **Infomaniak-specific** component, created by the devs.
- **Colors** freely configurable.

## Badges

- No issues Figma/Dev. Refer to the Material documentation if needed.

## Buttons

- Provide the **raw icons** for the different sizes depending on the stroke — **variable strokes**
  are reserved for web.
- **Button group** = buttons combined together.
  - Design side: prefer it as soon as several buttons are used (recommended, not mandatory).
  - Dev side: handles **toggle buttons** automatically (animation, etc.).
- **FAB** = reserved for a primary action at the bottom right; otherwise, they are simple
  **icon buttons**.
- Refer to the Material documentation if needed for the rest.

## Cards

- The component **does not exist as-is on the Android side** — to be built by the devs.
- Easily replicable structure, but **not callable by default** in this form.
- The devs only have the **slot version**.

## Carousel

- No issues Figma/Dev. Refer to the Material documentation if needed.

## Checkbox

- **Extended colors** can be used beyond the default ones.

## Chips

- Like the buttons: prefer the **chip group** as soon as several chips are used, for better dev
  integration.
- Refer to the Material documentation if needed for the rest.

## Date & Time Picker

- Either **reused as-is**, or **rebuilt from scratch** — the existing Calendar cells cannot be used
  directly, the devs will have to recode them.
- Icons **cannot be replaced** with ours.
- The **input** is a component separate from the date/time picker, to keep our calendar icon and
  avoid visual differences in a form.

## Dialogs

- **Dialog**: max 2 actions — adding more is discouraged (otherwise manual development).
- **List dialog**: fully custom — can contain something other than a list (image, etc.).
- One of the actions can be **destructive**, even though this is not natively available in the
  component.

## Dividers

- **Divider + Subheader** does not exist in code — to be rebuilt manually.
- Refer to the Material documentation if needed for the rest.
- ⚠️ Action item: improve the Material component to create a dedicated set.

## Lists

- **Icons** can be replaced with our own (icon or chevron).
- **Swipe actions** can be modified, **max 3**.
- No background by default, but one can be added.

## Loading & Progress

- No issues Figma/Dev. Refer to the Material documentation if needed.

## Menu

- **Icons** can be replaced with our own (icon or chevron).
- Refer to the Material documentation if needed.

## Navigation

- **Navigation rail**: tablet/desktop only. 📱💻
- **Navigation bar**: mobile or very small screens.
- **Drawer**: still used for some cases, despite being deprecated by Material.
- ⚠️ No long text: beyond that, the text is truncated with "…", which Material discourages.

## Radio Button

- No issues Figma/Dev. Refer to the Material documentation if needed.

## Search

- Reuses the **list items** → fully customizable.
- Refer to the Material documentation if needed.

## Shape

- Refer to the Material documentation if needed.

## Sheets

- **Side sheets** not available on Jetpack Compose for now (as of June 2026).
- ⚠️ Avoid overly experimental gradients: the content can be scrolled and the gradient risks being
  blocked by the handle.

## Sliders

- Refer to the Material documentation if needed.

## Snackbar

- Additional **colors** can be considered.
- No **illustrative icon**.

## Switch

- Refer to the Material documentation if needed.
- ❌ Size cannot be reduced — otherwise non-compliant with Material recommendations.

## Tabs

- ⚠️ Make sure to use the **primary** when there is no secondary.
- Refer to the Material documentation if needed.

## Text Fields

- **Filled version**: bottom edges not rounded (otherwise it masks part of the bottom border) →
  prefer the **outline version** for fully rounded edges.
- The chosen style must be **consistent across the entire app**.
- **Corner radius** can be modified if needed (e.g.: 4 → 8).
- **Icons** customizable (e.g.: search).
- Refer to the Material documentation if needed.

## Toolbars

- Reserved for **actions**; possible for secondary navigation, otherwise use a **nav bar**.
- No mix of tab + standalone icon — for tab + icon, apply the toolbar and the FAB separately on the
  right.
- Refer to the Material documentation if needed.

## Tooltips

- Refer to the Material documentation if needed.

## Utilities

- ❌ Cannot be edited.

---

## Quick summary

<Table
  headers={['Category', 'Components']}
  rows={[
    ['🟢 Fully customizable', 'Avatars'],
    [
      '🟡 Partially customizable (icons, colors, groups recommended)',
      'App Bars, Buttons, Checkbox, Chips, Lists, Menu, Snackbar, Search, Text Fields',
    ],
    [
      '🟠 As-is or to rebuild (full custom)',
      'Cards, Date & Time Picker, Dialogs (list dialog), Dividers, Navigation',
    ],
    ['🔴 Cannot be edited / constrained', 'Utilities, Switch (size), Date & Time Picker (icons)'],
    [
      '⚪ No issues / refer to Material',
      'Badges, Carousel, Loading & Progress, Radio Button, Shape, Sliders, Tabs, Toolbars, Tooltips',
    ],
    ['📱💻 Tablet/Desktop only', 'Navigation rail'],
  ]}
/>

# Designers Guide/Android/Exporting Token Updates

> This guide walks you through updating the Material color tokens in Figma and exporting them for the Android team. **N...

This guide walks you through updating the Material color tokens in Figma and exporting them for the
Android team. **Never export before an Android developer has approved the changes.**

---

## Before you start

Make sure you have:

- edit access to the [Material kit](https://www.figma.com/design/r4D2DKWIyzVoigyiTh16Hh/Edelweiss---Material-Kit?m=auto&t=6Praqzvd4yFcNUmT-6).
- access to the **[HCT Tonal Palette](hct-tonal-palette.md)** generator, our in-house tool (only needed if you create a new color palette).
- a Figma variables export plugin (e.g. [Variables Pro](https://www.figma.com/community/plugin/1264578192495051449/variables-pro-swap-import-export-variables)).
- an Android developer who will review your changes.

---

## Step 1: Create the new color palette (if needed)

Skip this step if you are only changing values in existing palettes.

1. Open the **[HCT Tonal Palette](hct-tonal-palette.md)** generator.
2. Enter the source color (hex) of the new palette.
3. Generate the full tonal palette, including tones you don't plan to use yet: Material roles rely on many different tones across all contrast modes.
4. Add the palette to the **Primitives** collection.
5. Name the new palette exactly like the existing ones: same structure, same tone steps. Do not rename or reorder existing palettes.

## Step 2: Apply the values following Material's logic

For each scheme, Material defines which tone of which palette each color role uses. Reproduce that mapping exactly: **do not adjust tones by eye**, even if a color looks slightly off.

- Example: in the default Light scheme, `primary` uses tone 40 of the primary palette. In the Dark scheme, it uses tone 80.
- Apply the mapping to **every mode** of the Theme collection (Light, Light medium contrast, Light high contrast, and their Dark counterparts). Tones change from one mode to another, so check each one separately.
- Theme values must **alias the Primitives variables**: never paste a raw hex value into Theme.
- Update the **Product** and **Dataviz** collections if your change affects them.

**Source of truth for the mapping:** [Material 3 - Color roles](https://m3.material.io/styles/color/roles)

If you are unsure about a mapping, ask an Android developer rather than guessing.

## Step 3: Get approval from an Android developer

Before exporting, always share the following with an Android developer:

- the new or modified palette,
- the tone-to-role mapping for each mode,
- screenshots of the main components affected, in Light and Dark.

## Step 4: Export the tokens

Only once your changes are approved.

1. Run the export plugin.
2. Select **only** these four collections:
   - **Primitives**
   - **Product**
   - **Theme**
   - **Dataviz**
3. Deselect every other collection, even if it seems related.
4. Export in `.json` format.

## Step 5: Hand off

1. Send the exported file to the related outputs mobile channel on kChat.
2. Add a short summary of what changed (new palette, modified roles, affected modes).

---

# Designers Guide/Android/HCT Tonal Palette

> Generates the tonal palette of a color in the [HCT color space](https://m3.material.io/blog/science-of-color-design)...

Generates the tonal palette of a color in the
[HCT color space](https://m3.material.io/blog/science-of-color-design) (Hue, Chroma, Tone), the
one used by Material Design 3. The hue and chroma of the source color are kept, only the tone
(perceived lightness, from `0` = black to `100` = white) changes.

1. Enter or pick the **base color**.
2. Adjust the **tones** to generate if needed.
3. Click a color to copy its HEX, or **Copy output** to copy the whole `tone  #HEX` list.

The **output background** only changes the preview, to check the swatches against a light or dark
surface.

<HctPaletteGenerator />

# Designers Guide/Figma Plugins

> Infomaniak's design system Figma plugins are distributed as zip files built automatically by CI on every merge to `de...

Infomaniak's design system Figma plugins are distributed as zip files built automatically by CI on
every merge to `develop`. They are installed locally in Figma Desktop as development plugins and
are not published to the Figma Community.

- **ESDS icons** — generates multi-size variants (16, 20, 24, 32, 40 px) of a 24×24px system icon.

---

## ESDS icons

The **ESDS icons** plugin generates multi-size variants of a 24×24px system icon (16, 20, 24, 32,
40 px). It is distributed as a zip file built automatically by CI on every merge to `develop` —
install it locally in Figma Desktop as a development plugin.

### 1. Download the plugin

Open the
[plugin releases page](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/releases?q=figma-plugin-icons)
and download the `esds-icons.zip` asset of the newest release.

### 2. Install it in Figma

Unzip the archive, then in Figma Desktop: **Plugins → Development → Import plugin from
manifest…** and select the unzipped `esds-icons/manifest.json`.

The plugin appears under **Plugins → Development → ESDS icons**. To generate the icon variants, follow the steps in the [icon contribution guide](../icons/icon-contribution.md#4-select-icon-and-run-esds-icons-plugin).

### Update the plugin

Download the latest zip, unzip it over the previous folder and reload the plugin in Figma
(**Plugins → Development → ESDS icons → Reload**).

---

# Designers Guide/Helpers/Creating a custom component

> Use this guide only when nothing can be reused from the native kit **and** the DS team has approved the creation of a...

Use this guide only when nothing can be reused from the native kit **and** the DS team has approved the creation of a custom component. If that approval hasn't happened yet, talk to the DS team before you start.

> 👑 **Golden rule**: don't do anything now that will have to be undone later. The component must be able to join its kit as is when it's integrated, without being taken apart.

## Which tokens for which component?

- 🍎 iOS/iPadOS component:
  [Token Core](https://www.figma.com/design/OgklXBGhUgpzlYPnVusMpw/Edelweiss---Token-Core?node-id=2-260&t=U8dJUATnrl0en4i0-11)
- 🤖 Material component:
  [Material kit](https://www.figma.com/design/r4D2DKWIyzVoigyiTh16Hh/Edelweiss---Material-Kit?m=auto&t=6Praqzvd4yFcNUmT-6)
- 🕸️ Shadcn component:
  [Shadcn kit](https://www.figma.com/design/eOY97TGxMkMx9ub9zt8e6v/Edelweiss---Shadcn-Kit--Paid-?m=auto&t=6Praqzvd4yFcNUmT-6)

<img
  src={CustomComponentTokens}
  alt="Applying kit tokens and text styles in Figma for Token Core, iOS/iPadOS, Material and Shadcn components"
/>

## 1. Design in context 🎨

1. Start with a simple frame in auto layout.
2. Place it in a real screen filled with real content. At this stage, it's not a component yet. The goal is to find the right shape first. Componentizing too early locks in things that will still change several times.
3. Once the component concept is set, validate it with the DS team and the dev teams to make sure it's feasible.
4. Once it's validated, convert it into a component, add all states and/or variants, then move on to step 2.

<img
  src={CustomComponentDesignInContext}
  alt="A calendar event designed in a real screen: ready for the DS team to approve vs one that shouldn't be a component at this stage"
/>

## 2. Test the edge cases 😥

- Very long text
- Empty content
- Variable widths
- Liquid Glass background for iOS/iPadOS 🍎

<img
  src={CustomComponentEdgeCases}
  alt="An event component with a very long title wrapping onto two lines instead of overlapping the trailing icons"
/>

## 3. Extract only when needed 🧩

- Create a subcomponent only if it has its own states or is reused elsewhere. Otherwise, keep a simple frame.
- For an internal subcomponent, prefix its name with `.` or `_`: Figma won't publish it to the library.

<img
  src={CustomComponentSubcomponents}
  alt="An internal _month-cell subcomponent reused as labels inside a calendar component"
/>

## 4. Ready-to-use component checklist ✅

### Tokens

- The tokens from its respective kit are applied
- The right tokens are used (e.g. no `background` token on text)
- No hard-coded values left (color, spacing, radius)
- Text styles are applied, not local sizes and weights
- The component is checked in light and dark mode
- Icons come from Iconography, with no imported or flattened icons

### Properties

- Default values are usable as is (default state, realistic text)
- Properties are properly named, in English
- Native kit naming is used whenever possible (e.g. symbol, leading, trailing…)
- Showing or hiding an element uses a boolean, not a variant
- Instance swaps offer preferred values (e.g. the relevant Iconography icons)
- Properties of nested instances are exposed when needed
- No unused or invalid properties left behind

### Structure

- No detached instances
- Auto layout is applied
- Layers are named (no "Frame 427"), with no hidden layers or leftover groups
- The component resizes correctly (hug and fill tested, min/max width if needed)
- Long-text behavior is defined (wrapping or truncation)
- Slots are used wisely (e.g. avoid multiple variants just to change how many times an element appears)
- Internal subcomponents are prefixed with `.` or `_`

## 5. Integration into the kit by the DS team 🌼

- All states required by the kit are present
- A usage doc explains why this component exists instead of a native equivalent

---

# Designers Guide/Install the Font

> Figma shows a warning when inspecting a text element that uses **Infomaniak Sans** if the font is not installed on yo...

Figma shows a warning when inspecting a text element that uses **Infomaniak Sans** if the font is
not installed on your computer. Installing the font locally fixes it.

## 1. Download the font files

Download the two TTF files from the [design-system repository](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/tree/main/packages/assets/fonts/fonts/infomaniak-sans):

- `infomaniak-sans.variable.normal.[opsz,wght].ttf`
- `infomaniak-sans.variable.italic.[opsz,wght].ttf`

## 2. Install with Font Book

Double-click each downloaded `.ttf` file. The macOS **Font Book** app opens a preview of the font,
click **Install**. That's it, the font is installed system-wide.

## 3. Restart Figma

If Figma was open, restart it. **Infomaniak Sans** now appears in the font picker and the missing-font warning is gone.

## Using the font on the web?

The web usage (CSS/HTML) is documented on the [Typography](../typography.md) page.

---

# Designers Guide/iOS/iOS - Technical Limitations

> **Goal:** identify which components can be modified and their related constraints.

**Goal:** identify which components can be modified and their related constraints.

---

## System

Hold actions:

- **Title** + **Description**: max 2 lines in standard use (avoid if possible), otherwise 1 line max.
- **Widgets** can be fully customized except for sizes (3 default sizes: see the kit)
- Display latency can go up to **15 min**

## Action Sheets

- Title, short description (single simple sentence), CTAs **Primary**, **Secondary**, **Destructive**.
- Controls must remain consistent across the entire app.
- ⚠️ No different **Primary** colors from one screen to another.

## Activity Views

- Only possible to **add actions**.

## Alerts

- Same as Action Sheets, with an additional **input field**.

## Buttons

- **Accent color** modifiable on the Primary only.
- To go further → build **fully custom** buttons, while staying close to the iOS style.
- **IC light** and **IC dark** values are handled by Apple (they add an extra layer).
- **Liquid Glass** — 3 available modes:
  - Colored Tinted
  - Colored Transparent Tinted
  - Transparent

## Color Picker

- ❌ Cannot be edited

## Contextual Menus

- **Very limited** customization.
- We can use **our own icons**.
- 💡 Jordan C. is a good reference on this component → reach out to him for any questions about its usage.

## Empty States

- On the dev side: called **"Content unavailable view"**.
- Contains: title, description, image, action.
- Rarely used.

## Face ID

- ❌ Cannot be edited

## Lists

### Header

- **Supertitle** and **Subtitle** are poorly handled in terms of backward compatibility → do not put critical information in them.
- **Nested** version: requires an action on the right in **text** form.

### Row swipe actions

- **Icons** and **actions** are modifiable.
- For the rest: check directly with the devs.

## Menus

- Same constraints as **Contextual Menus**.

## Notifications

- ❌ Cannot be edited

## Page Control

- ❌ Cannot be edited

## Pickers

- ❌ Cannot be edited
  > Useful for quick flows (e.g. simple event creation).

## Popovers

- 📱 **iPad only**.

## Pop-up Buttons

- **Accent color** modifiable only.

## Progress Indicators

- **Accent color** modifiable only.

## Segmented Controls

- Fully customizable (size, color…)

## Sheets

- **Grabber** present or not depending on needs, if the sheet can be dismissed via swipe.
- 3 heights enforced by Apple: **small**, **medium**, **large**, or adapt the sheet size to its content.
- **Inspector**: always slightly transparent (see the Maps app).
- **Full screen cover** = takes the entire screen, **no grabber**.
- **Close button strongly recommended** for accessibility; Apple provides a "cancellation zone" that adapts to the region (e.g. Arabic-speaking countries → left).

## Sidebar

- 📱 **iPad only**.

## Sliders

- **Accent color** modifiable only.
- Scale can be modified but with **linear steps**:
  - ✅ 5, 10, 15… or 10, 20, 30…
  - ❌ No random values (3, 7, 19…).

## Status Bar & Menu Bar

- ❌ Cannot be edited

## Steppers

- Either as-is, or **fully custom**. No in-between.

## Tab Bar

- Widths are **not stretchable** — use them as they are.
- Only **color** and **icon** are modifiable.
- 📱 On iPad: can be displayed at the top or the bottom → **prefer the top** (like Apple TV).

## Text Fields

- The **accent color bar** (input) is **unique across the entire app**, but specific zones can adapt it (e.g. **Euria** → blue).
- **List background colors**: easily modifiable.
- **Placeholders** use transparency → do not touch the colors.

## Toggle

- Either keep the component as-is, changing the green for a **brand color**.
- Or build a **fully custom** component (SwiftUI provides all the accessibility parameters for this).

## Toolbars

- It's possible to **force** large or small title display → but **prefer the native behavior**:
  - Large title that shrinks on scroll.
  - Small title when used in a sheet.
- **Accent color** is modifiable, nothing else.

## Widgets

- ❌ Cannot be edited

## Windows

- ⚪ Not applicable.

---

  ]}

# Design Tokens/Getting Started

> Our design system is powered by design tokens: name-value pairs that define the visual language of Infomaniak product...

<div className="welcome-section">
  <h1>Design Tokens</h1>
  <p className="welcome-description">
    Our design system is powered by design tokens: name-value pairs that define the visual language
    of Infomaniak products. Tokens ensure consistency across platforms while remaining flexible
    enough for different contexts.
  </p>
</div>

- [Token Architecture](#token-architecture)
- [Consuming Tokens](#consuming-tokens)
  - [Web](#web)
    - [Install from NPM](#install-from-npm)
    - [CSS Files](#css-files)
    - [Using `*.root.css` files](#using-rootcss-files)
    - [Using `*.attr.css` files](#using-attrcss-files)
      - [Import all contexts (all.attr files)](#import-all-contexts-allattrcss-files)
    - [Tailwind CSS V4](#tailwind-css-v4)
  - [LLM/AI](#llmai)
  - [iOS](#ios)
    - [Installation](#installation)
    - [Usage](#usage)
- [How It Works](#how-it-works)
  - [Token Resolution Chain](#token-resolution-chain)
  - [Modifiers Override by Path Matching](#modifiers-override-by-path-matching)

## Token Architecture

Our token system follows the Design Tokens Community Group (DTCG) standard with a three-tier architecture:

- <a href="t1.md">T1 Primitive tokens</a> for foundational tokens
  values
- <a href="t2.md">T2 Semantic tokens</a> for semantic abstraction
  tokens
- <a href="t3.md">T3 Component tokens</a> for component-specific
  tokens

## Consuming Tokens

### Web

#### Install from NPM

```bash
npm install @infomaniak-design-system/tokens
```

#### CSS Files

We offer two CSS file formats:

<Table
  headers={['File format', 'CSS Selector', 'Usage']}
  rows={[
    [
      <code>*.root.css</code>,
      <code>:root, :host</code>,
      <p>
        <code>*.root.css</code> files apply globally via <code>:root</code> immediately.
        <br />
        Use <code>media</code> queries with theme files to prevent conflicts (e.g., loading both
        light and dark simultaneously).
      </p>,
    ],
    [
      <code>*.attr.css</code>,
      <code>[data-esds-&lt;modifier&gt;="&lt;context&gt;"]</code>,
      <div>
        <p>
          <code>.attr.css</code> files only affect elements inside a container with the matching
          data attribute.
        </p>
        <ul>
          <li>
            <code>&lt;modifier&gt;</code>: "theme" | "product"
          </li>
          <li>
            <code>&lt;context&gt;</code>: "infomaniak" | "mail" | "euria" | ...
          </li>
        </ul>
      </div>,
    ],
  ]}
/>

#### Using `*.root.css` files

Root CSS files could be loaded using query, for example:

```html
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/tokens.root.css"
/>
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/modifiers/product/mail.root.css"
/>

<!-- Auto-switch based on system preference -->
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/modifiers/theme/light.root.css"
  media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)"
/>
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/modifiers/theme/dark.root.css"
  media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"
/>
```

#### Using `*.attr.css` files

Attr CSS file could be imported via CSS and activated using data attributes:

**NOTE**: `*.attr.css` CSS files are **optional** and should be imported only if necessary.

```css
@import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/tokens.attr.css';
@import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/modifiers/product/mail.attr.css';
@import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/modifiers/theme/dark.attr.css';
```

Modifiers can also be set on container elements:

```html
<body
  data-esds-theme="dark"
  data-esds-product="mail"
>
  <!-- Dark theme and product mail applies to children -->
</body>
```

##### Import all contexts (`all.attr.css` files)

Each modifier also generates an `all.attr.css` file which imports the attribute CSS of all its contexts at once, for example:

```css
@import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/modifiers/theme/all.attr.css';
```

#### Tailwind CSS V4

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/tokens.root.css';
@import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/tailwind.css';
```

```html
<button class="bg-brand-default">Click me!</button>
```

##### Namespace

Tailwind tokens are scoped by their respective namespace.
For example, `color.background.*` tokens are scoped to `bg-` classes, `color.content.*` tokens are scoped to `text-` classes, etc.

##### States

States may be applied to _background_ color tokens by suffixing a `bg-` token with `-state-[state-token-name]`.

_Example:_ `bg-brand-state-selected-strong` will apply the `color.state.selected-strong` state token to the `color.background.brand` background token.

Both are mixed to form a combined color that you may use to style the background of an element when it is in a specific state.

For the previous example, a common usage would be `active:bg-brand-state-selected-strong`.

### LLM/AI

Use the <a href="../ai-llms.md">AI &amp; LLMs</a> resources (`DESIGN.md`, `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`) to provide design system context to your AI agent or LLM. They contain a structured, machine-readable reference of the entire token system in a format optimized for AI consumption.

### iOS

#### Installation

Swift Package Manager — via Xcode or Package.swift:

```swift
swift.package(url: "https://github.com/Infomaniak/ios-design-system", branch: "main")
swift.target(
    name: "MyTarget",
    dependencies: [
        .product(name: "DesignSystem", package: "ios-design-system")
    ]
)
```

_Supported platforms: iOS 16+, macOS 13+, visionOS 1+_

##### Package structure

```
CatalogApp/               ← Demo app
Sources/DesignSystem/     ← Tokens, SwiftUI components
Tests/DesignSystemTests/  ← Unit tests
```

#### Usage

##### Configure environment

```swift
import DesignSystem

// Get theme via environment variable
@Environment(\.esdsTheme) var theme
```

##### Access tokens in **SwiftUI**

```swift
struct ContentView: View {
    @Environment(\.esdsTheme) var theme

    var body: some View {
        VStack {
            Text("Hello")
                .foregroundColor(theme.color.text.default)
                .padding(theme.spacing.medium)
        }
        .background(theme.color.background.default)
    }
}
```

##### Set theme

```swift
// In your app
@main
struct MyApp: App {
    var body: some Scene {
        WindowGroup {
            ContentView()
                .environment(\.esdsTheme, EsdsTheme.kdrive)
        }
    }
}
```

## How It Works

### Token Resolution Chain

Token values reference each other in a hierarchy, ensuring consistency across the system:

```
T3-Component  →  button.background.error
                    ↓
T2-Semantic   →  color.background.error.default
                    ↓
T1-Primitive  →  color.red.600 (#E21C40)
```

When a primitive value changes, every token referencing it updates automatically.

### Modifiers Override by Path Matching

Modifiers let you swap the values of existing tokens without changing their names. They work by matching the path of a T2 (semantic) or T3 (component) token and replacing its value for specific contexts.

**How it works:**

1. A modifier file contains the same token path as the base token
2. When applied, it replaces that path's value in the CSS cascade
3. Resolution continues with the new value

**Example**: The `euria` product modifier

The `euria.tokens.json` modifier overrides `color.background.brand` (the default brand background) by including the same path with a different value:

Base `t2-semantic/color.tokens.json`:

```json
{
  "color": {
    "background": {
      "brand": {
        "$root": { "$value": "{color.background.brand.infomaniak}" },
        "infomaniak": { "$value": "{color.blue.600}" },
        "euria": { "$value": "{color.ocean.700}" }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`modifiers/product/euria.tokens.json`:

```json
{
  "color": {
    "background": {
      "brand": {
        "$value": "{color.background.brand.euria}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**Resolution with modifiers:**

Multiple modifiers can be applied simultaneously. In the example below, the `euria` modifier points the brand background to the Euria brand token, then `dark` further adjusts it for the dark theme:

```
With data-esds-product="euria" data-esds-theme="dark":

              T3: button.background.color
                      ↓
              T2: color.background.brand
                      ↓
  Euria modifier: color.background.brand.euria (color.ocean.700)
                      ↓
   Dark modifier: color.background.brand.euria (color.ocean.400)
                      ↓
              T1: color.ocean.400
```

**Apply modifiers using data attributes:**

```html
<body
  data-esds-product="euria"
  data-esds-theme="dark"
>
  <!-- All children resolve with both modifiers applied -->
  <button style="background: var(--esds-color-background-brand)">
    Gets a color.ocean.400 background
  </button>
</body>
```

# Design Tokens/T1

> T1 tokens are the foundational design tokens that define the raw values of your design system. These are the base val...

## What are T1 Tokens?

T1 tokens are the foundational design tokens that define the raw values of your design system. These are the base values that don't reference other tokens.

### Characteristics:

- **Base values**: Colors, spacing, shadows, etc.
- **No references**: They contain actual values (hex colors, pixel dimensions)
- **Platform agnostic**: Represent the design intent without assumptions about usage
- **Source of truth**: Other tiers reference these values

### Token Categories in T1:

  headers={['Category', 'Description']}
  rows={[

    [
      <a href="t1/border-width.md">Border Width</a>,
      'Border thickness values',
    ],
    [
      <a href="t1/breakpoint.md">Breakpoint</a>,
      'Responsive breakpoints',
    ],
    [<a href="t1/color.md">Color</a>, 'Color palette'],
    [<a href="t1/dimension.md">Dimension</a>, 'Dimension values'],
    [<a href="t1/font.md">Font</a>, 'Typography tokens'],
    [<a href="t1/opacity.md">Opacity</a>, 'Opacity values'],
    [<a href="t1/radius.md">Radius</a>, 'Border radius values'],
    [<a href="t1/ratio.md">Ratio</a>, 'Aspect ratios'],
    [<a href="t1/shadow.md">Shadow</a>, 'Shadow effects'],
    [<a href="t1/spacing.md">Spacing</a>, 'Spacing values'],
  ]}

# Design Tokens/T2

> T2 tokens are semantic design tokens that reference T1 (primitive) values. They define aliases and common names to ab...

## What are T2 Tokens?

T2 tokens are semantic design tokens that reference T1 (primitive) values. They define aliases and common names to abstract the T1 tokens.

### Characteristics:

- **Purpose-driven naming**: Named by what they do, not what they are
- **Resolve to T1 values**: Point to primitive tokens for actual values
- **Modifiers**: Modifiers could override T2 tokens to adapt to a specific use cases
- **Cross-component usage**: Used by multiple components
- **Design patterns**: Semantic layer ensures consistent usage

### Examples:

- `color.background.primary` instead of `color.blue.500`
- `spacing.section.large` instead of `spacing.32`

### Token Categories in T2:

<Table
  headers={['Category', 'Description']}
  rows={[
    [<a href="t2/blur.md">Blur</a>, 'Semantic blur styles'],
    [<a href="t2/border.md">Border</a>, 'Semantic border styles'],
    [<a href="t2/color.md">Color</a>, 'Semantic color aliases'],
    [<a href="t2/font.md">Font</a>, 'Semantic typography'],
    [<a href="t2/icon.md">Icon</a>, 'Icon-related tokens'],
    [<a href="t2/opacity.md">Opacity</a>, 'Semantic opacity tokens'],
    [<a href="t2/radius.md">Radius</a>, 'Semantic border radius'],
    [<a href="t2/spacing.md">Spacing</a>, 'Semantic spacing'],
    [<a href="t2/text.md">Text</a>, 'Text styling tokens'],
    [<a href="t2/typography.md">Typography</a>, 'Typography tokens'],
  ]}
/>

# Design Tokens/T3

> T3 tokens are component-specific design tokens that reference T1 (primitive) and T2 (semantic) values. They define vi...

## What are T3 Tokens?

T3 tokens are component-specific design tokens that reference T1 (primitive) and T2 (semantic) values. They define visual properties for specific components.

### Characteristics:

- **Component-specific**: Named after a specific component
- **Reference T1 and T2**: Points to lower tier tokens
- **Modifiers**: Modifiers could override T3 tokens to adapt to a specific use cases
- **Single component usage**: Used by one specific component
- **Different variants**: Supports component states (hover, active, disabled)

### Examples:

- `button.background.hover` using `color.background.primary.hover`
- `card.padding` using `spacing.section.medium`

### Token Categories in T3:

<Table
  headers={['Category', 'Description']}
  rows={[
    [<a href="t3/badge.md">Badge</a>, 'Badge component tokens'],
    [<a href="t3/body.md">Body</a>, 'Body component styles'],
    [<a href="t3/button.md">Button</a>, 'Button component tokens'],
    [
      <a href="t3/heading.md">Heading</a>,
      'Heading component styles',
    ],
    [<a href="t3/kbd.md">Kbd</a>, 'Kbd component tokens'],
    [
      <a href="t3/separator.md">Separator</a>,
      'Separator component tokens',
    ],
    [
      <a href="t3/text-link.md">Text Link</a>,
      'Text Link component tokens',
    ],
  ]}
/>

# Design Tokens/CHANGELOG

> Consumers referencing the removed `--esds-color-border-dataviz-<hue>-dim1` / `-dim2` CSS custom properties must updat...

# Changelog

## 0.8.0 (2026-10-26)

### Minor Changes

- [#445](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/445) [`ea776ff`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/ea776ffdfadc49fcadf36a1f9a438b5bffcbd83d): Add the `esds-badge` web component and its design tokens.

  - New `esds-badge` component that renders a compact status badge around its slotted content (`role="status"`).
  - New `badge` component tokens (size, padding, radius, colors, font) and `badge-type` modifiers (`primary`, `neutral`).

### Patch Changes

- [#432](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/432) [`bb3203c`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/bb3203ce13aea5a2a8186d4658d4a92af5779078): Added a new `50` value to the scale token, usable for width/height sizing.

- [#460](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/460) [`3814fd1`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/3814fd1d10863a74ad7ec9f27f501d985fbb19c4): Added Tailwind CSS variables for icon sizes: semantic `icon.size` tokens are now exposed as `--text-icon-*` variables, so icon sizes can be applied through `text-icon-*` utilities.

- [#442](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/442) [`bf96e37`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/bf96e375d3b64abeed6855e0078e17febe0597da): Added `button.size` design tokens. Square `esds-button` elements are now sized by the design system (32 px for `small`, 40 px for `medium` — also the default — and 50 px for `large`) instead of a hardcoded 50 px fallback, so they previously ignored the selected `data-esds-button-size` and always rendered 50 px.

- [#455](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/455) [`ec0df07`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/ec0df0708ee2dfb8551a92842550e591a2513669): Publishing tokens to the iOS and Android repositories now deletes the previous `esds/tokens/*` branches from the same release channel (`rc`, `dev`, or prod), which also closes their pull requests.

- [#431](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/431) [`a2649a1`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/a2649a162f98f4fb9f00a2d644a2e6e7b46fa6a8): Added the "do not edit directly" auto-generated header to the Kotlin `build.gradle.kts` files, matching the other generated outputs.

- [#430](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/430) [`9f46096`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/9f46096020e13d5684a2c339a6e80f2fc63141b1): `esds-body` and `esds-heading` Tailwind typography classes are now defined as Tailwind v4 custom utilities (`@utility`) instead of component-layer classes. They can be combined with Tailwind variants (e.g. `hover:`, `md:`) and participate correctly in Tailwind's utility ordering. Class names are unchanged.

- [#440](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/440) [`ada09b1`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/ada09b14bf035fac732f74b39239112132e36261): Synced DTCG tokens with the latest Figma export: borders rendered on strong (dim1) feedback backgrounds are now transparent in both light and dark themes, instead of white in light theme and dark 950 shades in dark theme. Strong feedback surfaces no longer draw an outline. The theme modifier overrides for these borders were removed accordingly; the `color.border.on.feedback.*.dim1` token paths are unchanged.

## 0.7.0 (2026-10-14)

### Minor Changes

- [#414](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/414) [`27d9550`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/27d955011ecf63cec0a9e965f63381d516d44d12): Flatten feedback border tokens and add on-feedback border tokens.

  - Removed `color.border.feedback.{error,success,warning,information,neutral}.dim1` and `.dim2` tokens: each feedback border color is now a single token (`color.border.feedback.{error,success,warning,information,neutral}`), resolving to the former `dim1` (strong) value in both light and dark themes.
  - Added `color.border.on.feedback.{success,warning,error,information,neutral}.dim1`, `.dim2` and `.dim3` tokens for borders rendered on top of feedback backgrounds.
  - Updated the `secondary-destructive` button modifier to reference the flattened `color.border.feedback.error` token.

- [#407](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/407) [`31cebf9`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/31cebf93babc179b5272d055a69de650d77d2397): Kotlin tokens are now generated for Kotlin/Compose Multiplatform: sources are emitted in the `commonMain` source set (`src/commonMain/kotlin`) instead of `src/main/kotlin`, and theme modules' `build.gradle.kts` now declare their namespace inside a `kotlin { android { ... } }` block.

- [#411](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/411) [`2ded88c`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/2ded88cfe25973e73b2248dfa3361b68dee6434f): Removed the Material token tier. All Material-specific tokens and build outputs are gone, including the CSS files under `dist/web/css/material/` and the Material Theme Builder documentation page. Import the standard tokens instead (`dist/web/css/tokens.root.css`, `dist/web/css/modifiers/…`).

- [#412](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/412) [`1cce78b`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/1cce78bb54ccfec85ab21b61cf81fd6b60e0eb1c): Synced DTCG tokens from the latest Figma export. Data-viz border tokens were restructured to match the data-viz foreground structure:

  - `color.border.dataviz.<hue>` is now a single token (holding the former `dim1` value), replacing the `dim1`/`dim2` variants. Orange and yellow borders moved from the 600 to the 500 shade, aligning with their data-viz foreground colors.
  - Added `color.border.on.dataviz.<hue>.{dim1,dim2,dim3}` tokens for borders drawn on data-viz backgrounds: no border (`transparent`) on strong backgrounds, and theme-aware shades on soft (`dim2`) and subtle (`dim3`) backgrounds.

  Consumers referencing the removed `--esds-color-border-dataviz-<hue>-dim1` / `-dim2` CSS custom properties must update to the new token paths.

- [#404](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/404) [`98b912f`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/98b912f2415544cf5d1d6c68035e538461f02340): Tailwind tokens now ship state helpers: any `bg-` token can be suffixed with `-state-[state-token-name]` to blend a background color with a state color.

  _Example:_ `active:bg-brand-state-selected-strong` applies the `color.state.selected-strong` state token over the `color.background.brand` background token.

### Patch Changes

- [#408](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/408) [`50d1305`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/50d1305ca55dabc7295867c973562047b585d805): All button types now expose `color.state.hover` and `color.state.pressed` tokens: primary buttons blend the `medium` state intensity over their background, while secondary and ghost buttons use the `soft` intensity, so hover and pressed states can be applied consistently across button variants.

- [#405](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/405) [`d4153bf`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/d4153bf9698f01109b50d370ed429d82413789cd): Kotlin tokens now include opacity tokens, which were previously excluded from the generated output.

- [#406](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/406) [`fc0e48a`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/fc0e48ace2199df1c6a9574e6e9a8c38452f9d3d): Synced design tokens with the latest Figma export. Pressed overlays are now more pronounced (interaction opacity raised from 16% to 30%), the light-theme warning feedback background uses a softer orange, and the dark-theme surface color was lightened. Disabled secondary buttons now keep their border instead of losing it. New primitive alpha shades `color.gray.50-30` and `color.blue.900-30` are available, and semantic brand and data-viz tokens now reference their dedicated semantic tokens for more consistent theming.

## 0.6.1

## 0.6.0

### Minor Changes

- [#355](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/355) [`46ce53f`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/46ce53f6a87f66cc1ae58551d3c25ef8fe53db8a): Added emphasized typography styles for headings and body text. Text emphasis is now opt-in via a new `emphasized` attribute on the `esds-heading` and `esds-body` custom attributes, new `esds-heading-{xs..xl}-emphasized` and `esds-body-{xs..lg}-emphasized` utility classes, or automatically through `<strong>` content inside a styled element.

  The `heading.{xs..xl}.font` and `body.{xs..lg}.font` tokens now expose `base` and `emphasized` variants instead of a single value; the previous flat token path was removed, so consumers referencing it must update to one of the new variants (e.g. `body.md.font.base`). The corresponding CSS custom properties were renamed accordingly (`--esds-body-md-font` becomes `--esds-body-md-font-base` / `--esds-body-md-font-emphasized`). Headings no longer default to the emphasized typography style: they now render with the base style unless emphasis is applied.

- [#328](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/328) [`74ba77c`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/74ba77c0b11487f885660274d58a4bbab39b3179): Added the `esds-button` custom attribute, which applies the design system button styles to native `<button>` and `<a>` elements while preserving native behavior — links keep their navigation semantics and are exposed to assistive technologies as buttons with proper `aria-disabled` handling. It supports `disabled` and `loading` states, with variants selected through `data-esds-button-type` (`primary`, `secondary`, `ghost`, and their destructive variants) and `data-esds-button-size` (`small`, `medium`, `large`) attributes. The matching design tokens ship as new `button-size` and `button-type` modifiers plus button component tokens, importable per variant or all at once (e.g. `@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/modifiers/button-size/all.attr.css`).

- [#353](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/353) [`cc0b29f`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/cc0b29fe89f9da9975f8426d43b5380aea632c8e): Added the `esds-kbd` custom attribute, which styles native `<kbd>` elements as keyboard keys — extra-small emphasized body typography with muted content color on a surface background, rounded with a `md` radius and a subtle `dim3` border, all driven by design tokens. The attribute can only be used on `<kbd>` elements, preserving native semantics. The element lays its content out with a flex `gap` token: multi-key shortcuts stay within a single `<kbd esds-kbd>` element, wrapping the `+` separator in a `<span>` so the keys are evenly spaced (e.g. `<kbd esds-kbd>⌘<span>+</span>K</kbd>`).

- [#353](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/353) [`cc0b29f`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/cc0b29fe89f9da9975f8426d43b5380aea632c8e): Added the `esds-separator` component, which divides content horizontally or vertically. It exposes `role="separator"` semantics with `aria-orientation`, and can be removed from the accessibility tree with the `decorative` attribute. Its appearance is driven by the design tokens.

- [#356](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/356) [`92e9970`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/92e9970095127ae916eebdaa2f7795f1e094a327): Added a new `focus.border.offset` token (defaults to `spacing.2xs`), exposed as the `--esds-focus-border-offset` CSS custom property. The focus effect on `esds-text-link` now offsets its outline with this token, so the focus ring no longer overlaps the link text and can be tuned via the custom property.

- [#375](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/375) [`ae6dd7d`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/ae6dd7d2ed43a1d4921c42f628b202a06a9b78ea): Added a new `all.attr.css` output for each modifier, which imports the attribute CSS of all its contexts into a single file. Consumers can now import one file per modifier (e.g. `modifiers/button-size/all.attr.css`) instead of listing every context variant individually.

- [#365](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/365) [`a81efb7`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/a81efb7e54df053baaa2384cd3afb60b650f6ed4): Synced DTCG tokens from the latest Figma export.

  - Added subtle `dim3` data-viz variants: new `color.background.dataviz.*.dim3` backgrounds and matching `color.content.on.dataviz.*.dim3` foregrounds, plus per-hue `color.content.dataviz.*` foreground tokens, available in both themes and the dataviz overrides.
  - Softened the strong `dim1` data-viz backgrounds (`600` → `500` shades) and re-paired the `dim1`/`dim2` foregrounds placed on them for proper contrast in light and dark themes.
  - Feedback foregrounds on strong backgrounds are now white; the tinted shades moved to the `dim2` variants and new `dim3` foregrounds were added.
  - Lightened the `error`, `success`, `warning`, `information` and `neutral` interaction-state content colors (`700` → `600` shades; `warning` now `orange.500`).

- [#362](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/362) [`f1cbc10`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/f1cbc102707535eb8b0869351eff9ce26e391812): Synced DTCG tokens from the latest Figma export.

  - Added `soft` overlay tokens for hover, pressed and selected states (`color.state.hover.soft`, `color.state.pressed.soft`, `color.state.selected.soft`), with light and dark theme values, backed by new 6% alpha primitives `blue.900-6` and `gray.50-6`.

### Patch Changes

- [#380](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/380) [`7bcc0ea`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/7bcc0eabc111ea6403e95a05a34221e5652149e9): Synced DTCG tokens from the latest Figma export.

  - Refreshed the `red` color ramp (all 10 shades updated to the new reds).
  - Darkened the strong (`dim1`) feedback backgrounds (`color.background.feedback.*.dim1`): `success`/`warning`/`error`/`information` moved one shade darker, `neutral` now `gray.500`.
  - Lightened the selected-state and focus overlays (`color.selected.*`): `20%/40%/80%` opacities replaced by `6%/12%/60%`, with matching theme shadow adjustments.
  - Swapped the light-theme elevated surfaces: `background.elevation.raised` is now `gray.50` and `background.elevation.overlay` is white.
  - Unified `color.border.dim1` to `gray.400` in both themes (previously `gray.500` in dark mode).

## 0.5.0

### Minor Changes

- [#250](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/250) [`c4a1614`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/c4a1614e0a9eeacb870becb5139c0a8b295aa918): Introducing `@infomaniak-design-system/fonts`, a new package distributing the Infomaniak Sans typeface (variable TTFs, woff2 files, and ready-to-use CSS), along with the tooling to build and publish font updates.

  The design system's base typography now uses Infomaniak Sans: the semantic `font.family.base` token points to the new `font.family.infomaniak-sans` primitive instead of Suisse Int'l.
  Load the fonts via own hosting to render text with the intended typeface.

Consumers referencing the previous flat token path must update to one of the new variants.

  Selected state overlay (`medium`) opacity increased from 12% to 40% for stronger selection feedback. New primitive blue shades (`900-20`, `900-40`) and an `xs` border-radius size are now available.

- [#320](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/320) [`c63aba2`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/c63aba26b422d7391d35b8f3ca4080fed78a55ce): Added new semantic feedback color tokens:

  - New `information` and `neutral` color groups across backgrounds (dim1, dim2, dim3), foregrounds, borders, and interaction states, available in both light and dark themes.
  - New `dim3` (subtle) background variants for the `success`, `warning`, and `error` feedback colors.

- [#308](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/308) [`b59d9bd`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/b59d9bd4f74ad883d877c4bd799113c35366d262): Separate Tailwind CSS v4 integration: the `tailwind.css` stylesheet maps all design tokens to Tailwind theme namespaces (`--color-*`, `--font-*`, `--text-*`, `--font-weight-*`, `--tracking-*`, `--radius-*`, `--blur-*`) via `@theme inline`. New `esds-heading-*` and `esds-body-*` utility classes are also available to apply typography text styles directly through Tailwind.

- [#310](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/pull/310) [`9e6f59c`](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/commit/9e6f59c5bcef0b330c1edf57a155cb0f6911e0ca): Restructured the semantic color tokens: removed the `default`, `hover`, `pressed`, and `selected` interaction states from background, border, content, and brand tokens. The previous `default` value now lives directly on the token (e.g. `color.background.elevation.sunken` instead of `color.background.elevation.sunken.default`). Consumers must update any references to the removed state variants.

  Introduced a `$root` token concept for shared base values across themed tokens, with matching export support in the Figma and Swift build outputs.

  Added new semantic background tokens: per-product brand colors (including Euria), feedback colors (success, warning, error) with `dim1`/`dim2` variants, and data-visualization backgrounds across hues.

  Added new alpha-variant primitive colors (e.g. `color.blue.50-12`, `color.blue.900-80`).

  Removed the unused `shadow.0` primitive token and simplified the text-link component tokens to `content.color.default` and `content.color.visited`.

## 0.3.0

### Minor Changes

- 2b185c3: Improved Tailwind token generation to map color tokens to their corresponding Tailwind utilities. Color tokens prefixed with `background`, `border`, and `content` now generate `background-color-*`, `border-color-*`, and `text-color-*` utility classes respectively, instead of the generic `color-*` class, producing more idiomatic Tailwind output.
- 6c2a24e: Split the T3 `typography` token set into separate `body` and `heading` component tokens, and introduced a new T2 `typography` set covering sizes `xs`–`5xl` with `base` and `emphasized` weight variants. Added typography documentation with a font preview component. Fixed a missing `error.dim1.default` color token in light and dark themes.

## Naming Conventions

All icons follow the `<prefix>:<name>` format (e.g., `esds:home`).

> For detailed naming guidelines, see the [internal icons documentation](https://infomaniak.pages.infomaniak.com/handbook/activites/frontend/convention-nommage-icones/).

## Web

### Optical Sizing

We are dynamically adjusting our SVG `stroke-width` based on the rendered size:

<Table
  headers={['Size', 'Dynamic stroke-width', 'Fixed 1.75px stroke-width']}
  rows={[
    [
      '24px',
      <svg
        key="dyn-24"
        width="1em"
        height="1em"
        viewBox="0 0 24 24"
        style={{ fontSize: '24px', display: 'inline-block' }}
      >
        <path
          fill="none"
          stroke="currentColor"
          stroke-linecap="round"
          stroke-linejoin="round"
          stroke-width="calc((1em / 32) + 1px)"
          vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"
          d="M3 11h3a2 2 0 012 2v3a2 2 0 01-2 2H5a2 2 0 01-2-2zm0 0a9 9 0 1118 0m0 0v5m0-5h-3a2 2 0 00-2 2v3a2 2 0 002 2h1a2 2 0 002-2m0 0v2a4 4 0 01-4 4h-5"
        />
      </svg>,
      <svg
        key="fix-24"
        width="1em"
        height="1em"
        viewBox="0 0 24 24"
        style={{ fontSize: '24px', display: 'inline-block' }}
      >
        <path
          fill="none"
          stroke="currentColor"
          stroke-linecap="round"
          stroke-linejoin="round"
          stroke-width="1.75"
          d="M3 11h3a2 2 0 012 2v3a2 2 0 01-2 2H5a2 2 0 01-2-2zm0 0a9 9 0 1118 0m0 0v5m0-5h-3a2 2 0 00-2 2v3a2 2 0 002 2h1a2 2 0 002-2m0 0v2a4 4 0 01-4 4h-5"
        />
      </svg>,
    ],
    [
      '48px',
      <svg
        key="dyn-48"
        width="1em"
        height="1em"
        viewBox="0 0 24 24"
        style={{ fontSize: '48px', display: 'inline-block' }}
      >
        <path
          fill="none"
          stroke="currentColor"
          stroke-linecap="round"
          stroke-linejoin="round"
          stroke-width="calc((1em / 32) + 1px)"
          vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"
          d="M3 11h3a2 2 0 012 2v3a2 2 0 01-2 2H5a2 2 0 01-2-2zm0 0a9 9 0 1118 0m0 0v5m0-5h-3a2 2 0 00-2 2v3a2 2 0 002 2h1a2 2 0 002-2m0 0v2a4 4 0 01-4 4h-5"
        />
      </svg>,
      <svg
        key="fix-48"
        width="1em"
        height="1em"
        viewBox="0 0 24 24"
        style={{ fontSize: '48px', display: 'inline-block' }}
      >
        <path
          fill="none"
          stroke="currentColor"
          stroke-linecap="round"
          stroke-linejoin="round"
          stroke-width="1.75"
          d="M3 11h3a2 2 0 012 2v3a2 2 0 01-2 2H5a2 2 0 01-2-2zm0 0a9 9 0 1118 0m0 0v5m0-5h-3a2 2 0 00-2 2v3a2 2 0 002 2h1a2 2 0 002-2m0 0v2a4 4 0 01-4 4h-5"
        />
      </svg>,
    ],
  ]}
/>

During the SVG build process, all stroke-widths are replaced with a relative formula and the `vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"` attribute is added so stroke width stays consistent regardless of scaling:

```
stroke-width="calc((1em / 32) + 1px)"
vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"
```

This gives the following approximate stroke-widths:

- **24px** icon → **1.75px** stroke-width
- **32px** icon → **2px** stroke-width
- **40px** icon → **2.25px** stroke-width
- ...

See the [implementation](https://github.com/Infomaniak/design-system/blob/develop/packages/assets/images/svg/scripts/shared/svg/iconify/build-svg-set-from-svg-directory/apply-optical-sizes.ts) for more details.

## iOS (SF Symbols)

Icons are also delivered to iOS as [custom SF Symbols](https://developer.apple.com/sf-symbols/). During the Figma import, an **outlined** version of each icon (filled paths, no strokes — a requirement of SF Symbols) is committed alongside the web SVG and feeds the generation of the `ESDSSymbols.xcassets` catalog published to the `ios-design-system` repository.

Symbols follow the same naming convention with the `esds-` prefix (e.g. `Image("esds-home")` in SwiftUI).

# Typography

> This page describes the typography basics of the design system.

This page describes the typography basics of the design system.

## Font Family

The main font family is "**Infomaniak Sans**".

It is available in different font weights.

<table>
  <tr>
    <td style={{ fontWeight: 'var(--esds-font-weight-regular)' }}>
      <FontPreview></FontPreview>
    </td>
    <td>font.weight.regular</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td style={{ fontWeight: 'var(--esds-font-weight-medium)' }}>
      <FontPreview></FontPreview>
    </td>
    <td>font.weight.medium</td>
  </tr>
</table>

> Installing the font locally to use it in Figma or another desktop app? Follow the
> [Install the Font](designers-guide/install-the-font.md) guide.

### Usage

The fonts are distributed by our S3 server: `https://fonts.storage.infomaniak.com/design-system/latest/infomaniak-sans.min.css`.

#### HTML

```html
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://fonts.storage.infomaniak.com/design-system/latest/infomaniak-sans.min.css"
/>
```

#### CSS

```css
@import 'https://fonts.storage.infomaniak.com/design-system/latest/infomaniak-sans.min.css';
```

### Applying the font

Use the CSS variable `--esds-font-family-base` to apply the font to the `<html>` element:

```css
html {
  font-family: var(--esds-font-family-base), sans-serif;
}
```

> It's a good practice to apply the font-family to the `<html>` element, as it allows you to later use a different font-family based on the user's language.
>
> ```css
> html[lang^='zh-'] {
>   font-family: var(--esds-font-family-zh), sans-serif;
> }
> ```

## Font Sizes & Line Heights

### Base Font Size

The default font size is `16px`. This corresponds to the CSS value of `1rem`.
Users are able to change the default font size in their browser.
By using `rem`, the font-sizes scale nicely with the user defined value.

### Tokens

[Text tokens](design-tokens/t2/text.md) (font sizes and line-heights) are defined by the `text.{xs..5xl}.{size|line-height|letter-spacing}` design tokens.

## Typography

[Typography tokens](design-tokens/t2/typography.md) group the font family, size, weight, etc. into a single token: `typography.{xs..5xl}.{base|emphasized}`.

It makes it easier to apply the expected font:

```css
font: var(--esds-typography-md-base);
```

## Elements

### Headings

Headings are used to break up content into sections to provide a clear hierarchy of information.

#### Custom attribute _(recommended)_

The [esds-heading](components/heading.md) attribute **must** be used to apply `heading` text styles to elements:

```html
<h1 esds-heading="xl">Large text</h1>
```

#### Tailwind

On projects using Tailwind-based UI elements, we provide the custom class `esds-heading-*` to apply `heading` text styles to elements:

```html
<h1 class="esds-heading-xl">Large text</h1>
```

For `emphasized` text, you may use the `esds-heading-{xs..xl}-emphasized` class.

#### Tokens

[Heading tokens](design-tokens/t3/heading.md) are defined by the `heading.{xs..xl}.{font}` design tokens, and are used by the `esds-heading` custom attribute.

Here's an example of how to apply raw styles:

```html
<h1 style="font: var(--esds-heading-xl-font)">Heading 1</h1>
```

### Body Text

Body texts are used as blocks or lines of text.

#### Custom attribute _(recommended)_

The [esds-body](components/body.md) attribute **must** be used to apply `body` text styles to elements:

```html
<p esds-body="md">
  This is a sample paragraph showing how text will appear in your application. It demonstrates the
  font style, size, and spacing that will be used throughout your content.
</p>
```

#### Tailwind

On projects using Tailwind-based UI elements, we provide the custom class `esds-body-*` to apply `body` text styles to elements:

```html
<p class="esds-body-sm">
  This is a sample paragraph showing how text will appear in your application. It demonstrates the
  font style, size, and spacing that will be used throughout your content.
</p>
```

For `emphasized` text, you may use the `esds-body-{xs..lg}-emphasized` class.

#### Tokens

[Body tokens](design-tokens/t3/body.md) are defined by the `body.{xs..lg}.{font}` design tokens, and are used by the `esds-body` custom attribute.

Here's an example of how to apply raw styles:

```html
<p style="font: var(--esds-body-md-font)">
  This is a sample paragraph showing how text will appear in your application. It demonstrates the
  font style, size, and spacing that will be used throughout your content.
</p>
```

### Text styles

# AI & LLMs

> The design system publishes machine-readable resources so AI agents, coding assistants and LLMs can consume accurate,...

The design system publishes machine-readable resources so AI agents, coding assistants and LLMs
can consume accurate, up-to-date documentation:

- [llms.txt](./llms.txt) — lightweight index and router: global coding rules plus categorized
  links to every documentation page. Start here for agent discovery.
- [llms-full.txt](./llms-full.txt) — the complete documentation in a single file (includes
  DESIGN.md), for one-shot ingestion (Cursor `@Docs`, RAG pipelines, chat uploads).
- [DESIGN.md](./DESIGN.md) — machine-readable token reference generated from our token
  definitions, in a format optimized for AI consumption.

# Components/Getting Started

> Reusable web components built for Infomaniak products. Each component is framework-agnostic and can be used in any pr...

<div className="welcome-section">
  <h1>Components</h1>
  <p className="welcome-description">
    Reusable web components built for Infomaniak products. Each component is framework-agnostic and
    can be used in any project that supports custom elements.
  </p>
</div>

## Installation

```bash
npm install @infomaniak-design-system/components
```

## Quick Start

Import and register the components you need. **Call `define()` in your application's entry file** (e.g., `main.ts`) so custom elements are defined before we try to render them:

```ts
import { EsdsIconComponent } from '@infomaniak-design-system/components';

EsdsIconComponent.define();
```

Use it in your HTML or JSX:

```html
<esds-icon name="esds:headset"></esds-icon>
```

> Each component may have additional configuration. See the component's documentation for specifics.

## Framework Support

Components are built as standard Web Components and work in any framework (React, Vue, Angular, vanilla JS, etc.). No additional adapters are required.

### React

Import the components you need from `@infomaniak-design-system/components`, and they are ready to use, with autocompletion.

### Angular

Add `schemas: [CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA]` to any Angular module or component that uses the Design System components:

```ts
import { CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA } from '@angular/core';

@Component({
  // ...
  schemas: [CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA],
})
```

## IDE Support

> ℹ️ IDE support is only needed if your framework does not already provide autocompletion.

The integration files are shipped in the package. Custom attributes (e.g. `esds-button` on a native `<a>` or `<button>`) are autocompleted on any element.

### JetBrains

JetBrains IDEs detect the components automatically through the `web-types` field of the package — no configuration is needed.

### VS Code

If you don't have one already, create a `.vscode/settings.json` file at the root of your project.

Then add or append the following configuration:

```json
{
  "html.customData": [
    "./node_modules/@infomaniak-design-system/components/vscode.html-custom-data.json"
  ],
  "css.customData": [
    "./node_modules/@infomaniak-design-system/components/vscode.css-custom-data.json"
  ]
}
```

# Components/Badge

> Import and register the custom element `esds-badge`:

- [Figma ↗](https://www.figma.com/design/OgklXBGhUgpzlYPnVusMpw/Edelweiss---Token-Core?node-id=2671-6&p=f&t=0Y9wp336CpvkcrCz-0)

## Usage

Import and register the custom element `esds-badge`:

```ts
import { EsdsBadgeComponent } from '@infomaniak-design-system/components';

EsdsBadgeComponent.define();
```

```html
<esds-badge>3</esds-badge>
```

## Description

Represents a badge. If no content is provided, the badge will be compacted as a small _dot_.

### Styles

#### Types

List of all available badge types:

- `primary` (default): primary style
- `neutral`: neutral style

##### Import

To import all badge types:

```css
@import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/modifiers/badge-type/all.attr.css';
```

Or individually:

```css
@import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/modifiers/badge-type/[type].attr.css';
/* example: @import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/modifiers/badge-type/primary.attr.css'; */
```

##### Apply

Add the attribute `data-esds-badge-type="[type]"` to apply a badge type:

```html
<esds-badge data-esds-badge-type="primary">3</esds-badge>
```

## Demo

## API

### Slots

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
|  | — | — | No | Contains the content of the badge. |

## Examples

### Default

```html
<esds-badge default-slot="3"></esds-badge>
```

### Empty

```html
<esds-badge></esds-badge>
```

# Components/Body

> Import and register the custom attribute `esds-body`:

## Usage

Import and register the custom attribute `esds-body`:

```ts
import { EsdsBodyAttr } from '@infomaniak-design-system/components';

EsdsBodyAttr.define();
```

```html
<p esds-body="md">Body</p>
```

## Description

A custom attribute for applying body text styles to elements while preserving native semantics.

Use the `<strong>` element to emphasize text within a body text element, or use the `emphasized` attribute on the `esds-body` attribute to apply emphasized styles to the text.

## Demo

## API

### CSS Custom Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| --esds-body-margin-block | — | — | No | The "block" margin to apply to the element (default: 0, only available for p). |
| --esds-body-margin-inline | — | — | No | The "inline" margin to apply to the element (default: 0, only available for p). |

## Examples

### Default

```html
<esds-body text="This is a body example" size="md"></esds-body>
```

### With Strong Content

```html
<p
      esds-body="md"
    >
      This is a body example <strong>with strong content</strong>
    </p>
```

### All Sizes

```html
<esds-body text="This is a body example"></esds-body>
```

# Components/Button

> Import and register the custom attribute `esds-button`:

- [Figma ↗](https://www.figma.com/design/OgklXBGhUgpzlYPnVusMpw/Edelweiss---Token-Core?node-id=1473-1429&t=ZWopR2KZ2XXD2MTX-0)

## Usage

Import and register the custom attribute `esds-button`:

```ts
import { EsdsButtonAttr } from '@infomaniak-design-system/components';

EsdsButtonAttr.define();
```

```html
<button esds-button>Button</button>
```

```html
<a
  esds-button
  href="#"
>
  Button link
</a>
```

## Description

Adding the custom attribute `esds-button` to a `<button>` or `<a>` element, applies the `esds-button` styles to this element.

### Styles

#### Types

List of all available button types:

- `primary` (default): for a primary button
- `primary-destructive`: for a destructive button
- `secondary`: for a secondary button
- `secondary-destructive`: for a secondary destructive button
- `ghost-primary`: for a ghost button
- `ghost-secondary`: for a ghost secondary button
- `ghost-destructive`: for a ghost destructive button

##### Import

To import all button types:

```css
@import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/modifiers/button-type/all.attr.css';
```

Or individually:

```css
@import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/modifiers/button-type/[type].attr.css';
/* example: @import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/modifiers/button-type/primary.attr.css'; */
```

##### Apply

Add the attribute `data-esds-button-type="[type]"` to apply a button type:

```html
<button
  esds-button
  data-esds-button-type="primary"
>
  Button
</button>
```

#### Sizes

List of all available button sizes:

- `small`: for a small button
- `medium` (default): for a medium button
- `large`: for a large button

##### Import

To import all button sizes:

```css
@import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/modifiers/button-size/all.attr.css';
```

Or individually:

```css
@import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/modifiers/button-size/[size].attr.css';
/* example: @import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/modifiers/button-size/small.attr.css'; */
```

##### Apply

Add the attribute `data-esds-button-size="[size]"` to apply a button size:

```html
<button
  esds-button
  data-esds-button-size="medium"
>
  Button
</button>
```

Both `data-esds-button-type` and `data-esds-button-size` can be combined:

```html
<button
  esds-button
  data-esds-button-type="primary"
  data-esds-button-size="medium"
>
  Button
</button>
```

## Demo

## API

### Attributes

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| disabled | — | — | No | Disables the button |
| loading | — | — | No | Displays a loading state on the button |

## Examples

### Button

```html
<esds-button content="Text content" buttonType="primary" size="medium"></esds-button>
```

### Link

```html
<esds-button content="Link content" href="https://infomaniak.com"></esds-button>
```

### Text Only

```html
<esds-button content="Text content"></esds-button>
```

### Types

```html
<esds-button></esds-button>
```

### Sizes

```html
<esds-button></esds-button>
```
